sources.entry: Tracks - Web-based application to help you implement David Allen’s Getting Things Done™ methodology. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Ruby

summary.one_liner: Tracks is a web-based, Ruby on Rails application for implementing David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD) methodology.
summary.what_it_does: The README is short and mostly points elsewhere: full installation and upgrade instructions live in the project wiki, and development and contributing details are also in the wiki and in CONTRIBUTING.md. It describes Tracks as a GTD-compatible web application built with Ruby on Rails. It names a principal maintainer, Jyri-Petteri "ZeiP" Paloposki, who sponsors the work through Ardcoras oy and offers paid consulting and a hosted version. The README does not list specific features such as contexts, projects, or review workflows, so those are not confirmed here. The listing on awesome-selfhosted describes it as a web-based tool for GTD task management and to-do lists.
use_cases: Managing personal to-do lists with GTD methodology
Self-hosting a task manager in a web browser
Organizing next actions and projects using David Allen's GTD system
Running a Ruby on Rails task management app
how_to_run: Read the installation instructions in the project wiki (the README defers setup to the wiki)
Back up your data before installing or upgrading
notable: Implements David Allen's Getting Things Done methodology as a web app
Hosted version offered by the principal maintainer as a way to support development
Detailed install and upgrade docs are kept in the project wiki
caveats: README is brief and defers setup, upgrade, and development details to the wiki
Project homepage, manual, and hosted-service links are blank in the README
Maintainer offers a paid hosted version and paid consulting
